# queue commands

Every `queue` command, with the arguments and options the console actually defines.

## `queue:failed`

List dead letters and queue depth; retry with queue:retry.

```bash
bin/semitexa queue:failed
```

| option | takes a value |
|---|---|
| `--transport` | yes |
| `--queue` | yes |
| `--limit` | yes |
| `--payload` | no |
| `--json` | no |

## `queue:retry`

Retry (or --forget) a dead letter by id, or --all of a queue.

```bash
bin/semitexa queue:retry ["id"]
```

| option | takes a value |
|---|---|
| `--queue` | yes |
| `--transport` | yes |
| `--all` | no |
| `--forget` | no |
| `--dry-run` | no |

## `queue:stats`

Throughput, failures, wait and run time per queue, and what is waiting now.

```bash
bin/semitexa queue:stats
```

| option | takes a value |
|---|---|
| `--transport` | yes |
| `--queue` | yes |
| `--window` | yes |
| `--json` | no |

## `queue:work`

Run a queue worker (processes queued listeners and handlers enqueued with execution: queued)

```bash
bin/semitexa queue:work ["transport"] ["queue"]
```

| option | takes a value |
|---|---|
| `--timeout` | yes |
